utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-08-91-A, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could I have appearances. Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELMORE
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Elizabeth Elmore on behalf of the Prosecution. I'm here today with senior appeals counsel Laurel Baig and case manager Colin Nawrot. Also with us today are appeals interns Hyuree Kim and Lindsay Cumming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Appearances for Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Slobodan Zecevic appearing for Mr. Stanisic this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And appearances for Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Dragan Krgovic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we proceed, I just want to make sure that both appellants can follow the proceedings in a language that they can understand. Mr. Stanisic, I address myself to you first. Are you able to follow the proceedings and understand them?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STANISIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zupljanin, are you able to follow the proceedings and understand them?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not receiving interpretation, Your Honour, so I'm not sure what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could someone please check that he is on the right channel to start with, and I will continue speaking. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So I have a question for you, Mr. Zupljanin. I just want to make sure that you can follow the proceedings in a language that you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can follow the proceedings in a language that I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This Status Conference is called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Sub-rule (B) of Rule 65 bis requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a notice of appeal, and thereafter within 120 days after the last Status Conference. The reason is to allow -- or the purpose is to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto and including also the mental and physical condition of that person. In the present case, the parties filed their notices of appeal on 13th May 2013 and the first Status Conference was held on 4th September 2013. The second to sixth Status Conferences were held on 11th December 2013, 9th April 2014, 24th July 2014, and 12th November 2014, and 9th March 2015 respectively. Today's Status Conference is the seventh in this case and was scheduled pursuant to an order issued by myself on the 14th of May, 2015. Now the first part of today's agenda relates to the detention conditions and health -- possible health issues of appellants. Thus I would like to inquire into the status of your detention conditions and health situation, Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Zupljanin. I will start with you, Mr. Stanisic. If you have any concerns in relation to the conditions of your detention or your state of health, I would invite you to raise them now. And if you prefer, this discussion can take place in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STANISIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we do not need a private session. The situation has not changed since last time. It's such that I can stand it and there is nothing special that I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Zupljanin, if you have any concerns in relation to the conditions of your detention or your state of health, please speak now. If you would prefer, this discussion can take place in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need to go to a private session. Everything is regular, unchanged, everything continues as it has until now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I will go to the next item which is the recent procedural history. I know that this is -- contains nothing new as far as you are concerned, but one of the reasons of a Status Conference is also to inform the general public and those who are following us. Before turning to any issues that the parties may wish to raise, I will outline the recent procedural history of this case, focusing on decisions and orders issued since the last Status Conference held on the 9th of March of this year. Indeed, one of the purposes of a Status Conference is to inform people outside the Tribunal of what is happening in a particular case, even though this information, as I have just stated, is already known by the parties. First, with regard to the composition of the Appeals Chamber seized of the present case, I recall that on the 22nd of April of this year, the President of the Tribunal appointed Judge Christoph Fluegge, Judge Fausto Pocar, and Judge Liu Daqun to replace Judge Arlette Ramaroson, Judge Khalida Khan, and Judge Bakhtiyar Tuzmukhamedov on the Bench respectively. The parties and public may be wondering why these further changes to the Bench were made. The reason is a very simple one. The three Judges who have been replaced are all Judges of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda. As the parties may be aware, the mandate of that Tribunal, the ICTR, and therefore the mandate of any ICTR Judges in the Appeals Chamber will come to an end by the end of the year of this year. When it became clear that this case would not conclude in 2015, it therefore became necessary to replace any ICTR Judge on the Bench with an ICTY Judge whose mandate will continue into 2016. I also recall that on the 20th of April this year, the Prosecution filed a confidential motion requesting that an exhibit be placed under seal. And the Appeals Chamber issued a confidential order granting the motion on 27th May 2015. This concludes my summary of the recent procedural history of this case. I come next to basically the last item of today's Status Conference agenda and that's issues raised by the parties. I would like to address myself first to the Prosecution. Do you wish to raise any issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELMORE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Only that the Prosecution would renew its request made at prior Status Conferences for as much notice as possible and at least eight weeks prior to the date of the appeal hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll do our best. We'll do our best, Ms. Elmore. The plans are to have the hearing done this year. Without committing myself, it probably will be in November, in November. Earliest it will be October, but it's more probable that we're talking of November. And then the case -- the appeal will be decided mid-next year. Our intention is to hand down the decision, the judgement, in June of next year.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELMORE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And so if there are any changes, we will of course inform you. Mr. Stanisic, do you have any issues you would like to raise? I'm asking him first.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STANISIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STANISIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, personally I have nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing. I would just like to emphasise that we join with the Prosecution for request for as earlier notice as possible, because both my co-counsel Mr. Bourgon and myself are committed to different trials and we would need to know in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but more or less you already know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will of course inform you, as I said, if there are changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zupljanin, do you wish to raise any issue?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT ZUPLJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing special to say. And as for the case, Mr. Krgovic will say anything that needs to be said and I fully trust him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zupljanin. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing from our side, Your Honour. We just join with the Prosecution request about the earlier announcement of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You heard me on that already. Unless there is anything else you would like to raise, I believe this concludes today's Status Conference. I thank the parties for their attendance and co-operation and call the proceedings to a close. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 9.43 a.m.
